stem.text: Water flows into a tank at a rate of R(t) liters per minute, where R is a differentiable function and t is measured in minutes. Measured values are R(0) = 4, R(2) = 7, R(5) = 9, R(10) = 6. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{10} R(t)\,dt \), the number of liters of water that flow into the tank from t = 0 to t = 10, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 2 \cdot \frac{4 + 7}{2} = 11 \); \( 3 \cdot \frac{7 + 9}{2} = 24 \); \( 5 \cdot \frac{9 + 6}{2} = \frac{75}{2} \).

distractor_derivations.B: trapezoidal sum with the common width (b - a)/3 used for every subinterval
distractor_derivations.C: factor 1/2 applied to the first trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.D: left Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
